questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle, doing simple harmonic motion, at a distance 3 cm from mean position has acceleration $12 \mathrm{ cm} / \mathrm{s}^2$. What is its time period?
questions.solution:
The time period of a particle executing SHM is
$T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{x}{a}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{\text{ Displacement }}{\text{ Acceleration }}}=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{3 \times 10^{-2}}{12 \times 10^{-2}}}=2 \pi \times \frac{1}{2}=\pi=3.14 $$\mathrm{ s}$

The amplitude of SHM is :

$\therefore \quad r^2\left(\cos ^2 \theta+\sin ^2 \theta\right)=3^2+4^2=25$ or $r=5 \mathrm{~cm}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two pendulums of time periods 3 s and 7 s , respectively start oscillating simultaneously from two opposite extreme positions. After how much time they will be in same phase?
questions.solution:
General equation of oscillation are
$\begin{aligned}
& y_1=A \sin \left(\omega_1 t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \\
& y_2=A \sin \left(\omega_2 t+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
\end{aligned}$
Now, $\omega_1 t+\frac{\pi}{2}=\omega_2 t-\frac{\pi}{2}$ or $\begin{aligned}
t & =\frac{\pi}{\omega_2-\omega_1} \\
& =\frac{\pi}{\left(2 \pi / T_2\right)-\left(2 \pi / T_1\right)} \\
& =\frac{T_1 T_2}{2\left(T_1-T_2\right)} \\
& =\frac{3 \times 7}{2(7-3)}=\frac{21}{8} \mathrm{ s}
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wave travelling in a stretched string is described by the equation $y=A \sin (k x-\omega t)$. The maximum particle velocity is :
questions.solution: $\begin{gathered}y=A \sin (k x-\omega t) \\ \frac{d y}{d t}=A \cos (k x-\omega t) \times(\omega) \\ \left(\frac{d y}{d t}\right)_{\max }=A(1)(\omega)=A \omega\end{gathered}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The path difference between the two waves $y_1=a_1 \sin \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}\right)$ and $y_2=a_2 \cos \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi\right)$ is
questions.solution:
$\begin{gathered} \text{ (b) } y_1=a_1 \sin \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}\right) \text{$ and $} \\ y_2=a_2 \cos \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi\right) \\ =a_2 \sin \left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi+\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \end{gathered}$
So, phase difference $=\phi+\frac{\pi}{2}$ and path difference $\Delta=\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi}\left(\phi+\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$

$y_1=4 \sin (\omega t+k x), \quad y_2=-4 \cos (\omega t+k x)$
the phase difference is

From Eqs. (i) and (ii), we get The phase difference, $\Delta \phi=\frac{3 \pi}{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two springs are connected to a block of mass $M$ placed on a frictionless surface as shown below. If both the springs have a spring constant $k$, then the frequency of oscillation of the block is
questions.solution:
The frequency of oscillation of a vibrating spring-block, system is given by
$v=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k_{\text{eff }}}{M}} \ldots$ (i)
Since, the springs are attached in series, each having spring constant $k$, so we have
$\frac{1}{k_{\mathrm{eff}}}=\frac{1}{k}+\frac{1}{k}=\frac{2}{k}\Rightarrow \quad k_{\text{eff }}=\frac{k}{2}$
From Eq. (i), we get $v=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k_{\text{eff }}}{M}}=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{2 M}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A simple pendulum oscillates in a vertical plane. When it passes through the mean position, the tension in the string is 3 times the weight of the pendulum bob. What is the maximum displacement of the pendulum of the string with respect to the vertical ?
questions.solution:
In mean position,
$\begin{aligned} T & =3 m g \\ \text{ Net force, } T-m g & =\frac{m v^2}{l}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}
& 3 m g-m g \\
\Rightarrow \quad & \frac{m v^2}{l} \\
v & =\sqrt{2 g l}
\end{aligned}$Let maximum displacement with respect to vertical is $\theta$, then
$\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{2} m v^2 & =m g h \\
& =m g(l-l \cos \theta) \\
\frac{1}{2} m(2 g l) & =m g l(1-\cos \theta) \\
\cos \theta & =0
\end{aligned}\Rightarrow \quad \theta=90^{{}^{\circ}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The path difference between two waves $y_1=a_1 \sin  \left(\omega$t-$\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}\right)$ and y_2=a_2 \cos$\left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi\right)$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $y_1=a_1 \sin  \left(\omega$ t-$\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}\right)$ and $y_2=a_2 \cos \left(\omega$ t-$\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi\right)=$ a_2 \sin $\left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\omega$ t-$\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi\right)\therefore Phase$ of first wave,\phi_1=$\left(\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}\right)$
and phase of second wave, $\phi_2=\frac{\pi}{2}+\omega t-\frac{2 \pi x}{\lambda}+\phi\therefore$ Phase difference, $\Delta \phi=\phi_2-\phi_1=\frac{\pi}{2}+\phi\begin{aligned} \therefore \text{ Path difference } & =\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi} \times \text{ phase difference } \\ & =\frac{\lambda}{2 \pi}\left(\frac{\pi}{2}+\phi\right)\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The two blocks of masses $m_1$ and $m_2$ are kept on a smooth horizontal table as shown in the figure. Block of mass $m_1$ but not $m_2$ is fastened to the spring. If now both the blocks are pushed to the left, so that the spring is compressed at a distance $d$. The amplitude of oscillation of block of mass $m_1$ after the system released, is
questions.solution:
Block of mass $m_2$ shoots off carrying some kinetic energy away from the system. To find its speed, potential energy of spring = maximum kinetic energy of blocks.
$\frac{k d^2}{2}=\left(m_1+m_2\right) \frac{v^2}{2}$
[ $k=$ force constant of spring]
$v^2=\frac{k d^2}{m_1+m_2}$ with $m_1$ along on the spring.
Maximum potential energy $=$ Maximum kinetic energy of $m_2\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & \frac{1}{2} k A^2=\frac{1}{2} m_1 v^2 \Rightarrow k A^2=\frac{k m_1 d^2}{m_1+m_2} \\ \Rightarrow & A=d \sqrt{\frac{m_1}{m_1+m_2}}\end{array}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sinusoidal wave travelling in the positive direction on stretched string has amplitude 20 cm , wavelength 1 m and wave velocity $5 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}$. At $x=0$ and $t=0$, it is given that $y=0$ and $\frac{d y}{d t} < 0$. Find the wave function $y(x, t)$.
options: $y(x, t)=(0.02 m) \sin \left[\left(2 \pi \mathrm{ m}^{-1}\right) x+\left(10 \pi \mathrm{ s}^{-1}\right) t\right] \mathrm{m}$
$y(x, t)=(0.02 m) \cos \left[\left(10 \pi \mathrm{ s}^{-1}\right) t+\left(2 \pi \mathrm{ m}^{-1}\right) x\right] \mathrm{m}$
$y(x, t)=(0.02 m) \sin \left[\left(2 \pi \mathrm{ m}^{-1}\right) x-\left(10 \pi \mathrm{ s}^{-1}\right) t\right] \mathrm{m}$
questions.solution:
We start a general form for a rightward moving wave,
$y(x, t)=A \sin (k x-\omega t+\phi)$...(i)
The given amplitude is $A=2 \mathrm{ cm}=0.02 \mathrm{ m}$
The wavelength is given as
$\lambda=1 \mathrm{ m}$
Wave number $=k=2 \pi / \lambda=2 \pi \mathrm{ m}^{-1}$
Angular frequency,
$\omega=v k=10 \pi \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
From Eq. (i),
$\because \quad \begin{aligned} y(x, t) & =(0.02) \sin [2 \pi(x-5 t)+\phi] \\ \text{ For } x & =0, t=0 \\ y & =0 \text{ and } \frac{\partial y}{\partial t} < 0\end{aligned}$
i.e. $\quad 0.02 \sin \phi=0$
(as $y=0$ )
and $\quad-0.2 \pi \cos \phi < 0$
From these conditions, we may conclude that $\phi=2 n \pi$, where $n=0,2,4,6, \ldots$
Therefore,
$y(x, t)=(0.02 \mathrm{ m}) \sin \left[\left(2 \pi \mathrm{ m}^{-1}\right) \mathrm{x}-\left(10 \pi \mathrm{ s}^{-1}\right) t\right] \mathrm{m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two particles executes SHM of same amplitude and frequency along the same straight line. They pass one another when going in opposite directions. Each time their displacement is half of their amplitude. The phase difference between them is
questions.solution:
Let two simple harmonic motions are $y=a \sin \omega t$ and $y=a \sin (\omega t+\phi)$
In the first case, $\frac{a}{2}=a \sin \omega t \Rightarrow \sin \omega t=\frac{1}{2}\therefore \quad \cos \omega t=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$In the second case, $\frac{a}{2}=a \sin (\omega t+\phi)\begin{aligned}
& \Rightarrow \quad \frac{1}{2}=[\sin \omega t \cdot \cos \phi+\cos \omega t \sin \phi] \\
& \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2}=\left[\frac{1}{2} \cos \phi+\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2} \sin \phi\right] \\
& \Rightarrow \quad 1-\cos \phi=\sqrt{3} \sin \phi \\
& \Rightarrow \quad(1-\cos \phi)^2=3 \sin ^2 \phi \\
& \Rightarrow \quad(1-\cos \phi)^2=3\left(1-\cos ^2 \phi\right)
\end{aligned}$On solving we get
$\begin{aligned}
& \cos \phi=+1 \text{$ or $} \cos \phi=\frac{-1}{2} \\
& \text{ i.e., } \quad \phi=0 \text{ or } \phi=120^{{}^{\circ}}
\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The angular velocities of three bodies in simple harmonic motion are $\omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3$ with their respective amplitudes as $A_1, A_2, A_3$ If all the three bodies have same mass and velocity, then
questions.solution:
Rate of change of displacement is known as velocity. The equation for displacment (y$ ) of a body in SHM with angular velocity \omega$ is given by
$y=a \sin \omega t$
where $\mathbf{a}$ is amplitude
velocity $v=$ rate of change of displacement $=\frac{d y}{d t}v=\frac{d y}{d t}=\frac{d}{d t}(a \sin \omega t)=a \omega \cos \omega t$
Given, $v_1=v_2=v_3$ and $a_1=A_1, a_2=A_2$.
$a_3=A_3A_1 \omega_1=A_2 \omega_2=A_3 \omega_3$

questions.solution: $y=k t^2\begin{aligned} \frac{d^2 y}{d t^2} & =2 k \\ a & =2 \mathrm{ m} / \mathrm{s}^2 \\ T_1 & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}} \\ T_2 & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g+a_y}} \\ \frac{T_1^2}{T_2^2} & =\frac{g+a_y}{g} \\ & =\frac{10+2}{10}=\frac{6}{5}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The acceleration of a particle performing SHM is $12 \mathrm{ cm} / \mathrm{s}^2$ at a distance of 3 cm from the mean position. Its time period is
questions.solution: Acceleration $a=\omega^2 y\begin{aligned} \Rightarrow \quad a & =\left(\frac{2 \pi}{T}\right)^2 y \\ \Rightarrow \quad T^2 & =\frac{4 \pi^2 y}{a} \\ \Rightarrow \quad T & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{y}{a}} \\ & =2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{3}{12}} \\ T & =2 \pi \times \frac{1}{2}=3.14 \mathrm{ s}\end{aligned}T=2 \pi \times \frac{1}{2}=3.14 \mathrm{ s}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass $M$ is attached to a string, oscillates with a period of 2 s. If the mass is increased by 4 kg. The time period increases by 1 s. Assuming, that Hooke's law is obeyed, the initial mass $M$ was :
questions.solution:
$T=2=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{M}{k}}$
and $2+1=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{M+4}{k}}$
or $3=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{M+4}{k}}\therefore \quad \frac{4}{9}=\frac{M}{M+4}$
or $4 M+16=9 M$
or $M=\frac{16}{5}=3.2 \mathrm{ kg}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two pendulums have time periods $T$ and $5 T / 4$. They start SHM at the same time from the mean position. What will be the phase difference between them after the bigger pendulum completed one oscillation?
questions.solution: When bigger pendulum of time period $\frac{5 T}{4}$ completes one vibration, the smaller pendulum will complete $\left(\frac{5}{4}\right)$ vibrations. It means the smaller pendulum will be leaded the bigger pendulum by phase $\frac{T}{4} \mathrm{sec}=\frac{\pi}{2} \mathrm{rad}=90^{{}^{\circ}}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mass $m$ hanging from a spring is doing simple harmonic motion with frequency $f$. If the mass is increased by 4 times, then frequency will be
questions.solution:
Frequency for a mass $m$ executing SHM
$f=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}$....(i)
When the mass is increased by 4 times, then the new frequency
$f^{\prime}=\frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{4 m}}=\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{2 \pi} \sqrt{\frac{k}{m}}=\frac{f}{2}$

when $A$ becomes twice $v_{\max }$ is also doubled.

questions.q: If two waves represented by $y_1=4 \sin \omega t$ and $y_2=3 \sin  \left(\$ omegat+$\frac{\pi}{3}\right)$ interfere at a point. The amplitude of the resulting wave will be about$
questions.solution:
Resulting amplitude of two interfering waves
$A=\sqrt{a_1^2+a_2^2+2 a_1 a_2 \cos \phi}$
Here, $\phi=\pi / 3, a_1=4, a_2=3\Rightarrow \quad A \simeq 6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two equal charges $q$ are kept fixed at $a$ and $+a$ alpng the $x$-axis. A particle of mass $m$ and charge $\frac{q}{2}$ is brought to the origin and given a small displacement along the $x$-axis, then
questions.solution:
From Coulomb's law
$\begin{aligned}
F & =\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q_1 q_2}{r^2} \\
F & =\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q \times \frac{q}{2}}{(a+x)^2}-\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q \times \frac{q}{2}}{(a-x)^2} \\
& =\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \frac{q^2}{2}\left[\frac{1}{(a+x)^2}-\frac{1}{(a-x)^2}\right] \\
& =\frac{1}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0} \cdot \frac{q^2}{2}\left[-\frac{4 a x}{\left(a^2-x^2\right)^2}\right]
\end{aligned}$
When $x< < a$, then
$\begin{aligned}
& F=-\frac{2 q^2}{4 \pi \varepsilon_0 a^3} x \\
\Rightarrow & F \propto-x
\end{aligned}$
Hence, SHM along $x$-axis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A function of time is represented as follows $\sin \omega t+\cos 2 \omega t+\sin 4 \omega t$. The motion represented by it is
questions.solution:
This is an example of a periodic motion. It can be noted that each term represents a periodic function with different angular frequency. Since, period is the least interval of time after which a function repeats its value, $\sin \omega t$ has a period
$T_0=\frac{2 \pi}{\omega}\cos 2 \omega t$ has a period $\frac{\pi}{\omega}=\frac{T_0}{2}$ and $\sin 4 \omega t$ has a period $\frac{2 \pi}{4 \omega}=\frac{T_0}{4}$
The period of the first term is a multiple of the periods of the last two terms. Therefore, the smallest interval of time after which the sum of the three terms repeats is $T_0$ and thus, the sum is a periodic function with a period $\frac{2 \pi}{\omega}$.
